dimensions.assessment: Affects consumers, financial institutions, credit reporting agencies, and state regulatory bodies nationwide by nullifying a federal preemption rule.
dimensions.evidence: rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to 'Fair Credit Reporting Act; Preemption of State Laws'

dimensions.assessment: Completely strips the specified federal rule of any force or effect, altering the legal relationship between federal and state credit reporting laws.
dimensions.evidence: Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to 'Fair Credit Reporting Act; Preemption of State Laws' (90 Fed. Reg. 48710 (October 28, 2025)), and such rule shall have no force or effect.

dimensions.assessment: Does not appropriate federal funds or directly set spending levels, though it may have indirect economic and regulatory compliance implications.
Uses statutory joint resolution authority under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, to nullify a formal federal administrative regulation.
dimensions.evidence: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection

dimensions.assessment: Permanent effect of rendering the targeted federal rule permanently void and without legal effect.
dimensions.evidence: such rule shall have no force or effect.

importance_detail.rationale: The joint resolution exercises congressional disapproval under the Congressional Review Act to invalidate a specific federal rule regarding Fair Credit Reporting Act state law preemption issued by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection.
